report_name: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack on M365

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: Attackers obtained and used a compromised OAuth application credential for the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application to gain initial access to Microsoft 365 tenants.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attackers used legitimate, stolen application credentials to authenticate, making their sign-ins appear as legitimate service-to-service communication and bypassing user-centric defenses like MFA.

attack_patterns.name: Additional Cloud Credentials
attack_patterns.description: In at least one observed case, attackers used their initial access to add new client secrets to other applications within the tenant, creating backdoors for persistent access.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Email Collection
attack_patterns.description: The compromised application's permissions gave attackers the capability to access and exfiltrate data from Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook email.

tools.name: ConnectWise Cloud Backup
tools.description: The legitimate cloud backup application whose credential was compromised and abused by attackers to gain unauthorized access to customer Microsoft 365 tenants.

tools.name: ConnectWise Cloud Management
tools.description: A related ConnectWise application that, in one observed case, had its privileges elevated to Global Administrator by the attackers after initial access.

campaigns.name: ConnectWise M365 Supply Chain Attack
campaigns.description: A supply chain attack where a compromised application credential for ConnectWise Cloud Backup was used to access customer Microsoft 365 tenants, bypassing MFA and allowing for privilege escalation and data access.

identities.name: ConnectWise
identities.description: IT management software provider whose Cloud Backup application credential was compromised and used as the vector for a supply chain attack.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Provider of the Microsoft 365 platform, which was the target environment accessed via the compromised application credential.

identities.name: Managed Service Providers (MSPs)
identities.description: A class of victims targeted in the attack, whose Microsoft 365 tenants and their downstream customers were compromised.

identities.name: Microsoft 365
identities.description: The cloud service environment that was compromised via the supply chain attack.

indicators.name: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack - Unauthorized Sign-in IP
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack - Unauthorized Sign-in IP
id: 9b1d8c3e-7f0a-4b1d-9c3e-8f0a7b1d8c3e
status: experimental
description: Detects sign-ins from an IP address associated with the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain attack in October 2026.
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/10/19/connectwise-cloud-backup-suspended-security-incident/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-19
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
level: high
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    IPAddress: '144.172.64.128'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects sign-ins from the IP address 144.172.64.128, which was observed by Huntress making unauthorized sign-ins during the ConnectWise supply chain attack.

indicators.name: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack - Compromised App ID Sign-in
indicators.pattern:
title: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack - Compromised App ID Sign-in
id: a2c3d4e5-f6a7-4891-8cde-f12345678901
status: experimental
description: Detects sign-ins from the compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application ID (506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae).
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/10/19/connectwise-cloud-backup-suspended-security-incident/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-19
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
level: high
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    AppId: '506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae'
  filter:
    IPAddress: '144.172.64.128' # Optionally filter for only the known bad IP
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Azure AD sign-ins from the application ID '506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae', which was compromised in the ConnectWise supply chain attack.

indicators.name: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack - Application Credential Addition
indicators.pattern:
title: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack - Application Credential Addition
id: b3d4e5f6-a7b8-4012-8def-123456789012
status: experimental
description: Detects an application adding new credentials to another application, a TTP observed in the ConnectWise supply chain attack for persistence.
references:
  - https://specterops.io/blog/2026/10/17/connectwise-skykick-breach-microsoft-365/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-19
tags:
  - attack.t1098.001
level: high
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName|contains:
      - 'Add service principal credential'
      - 'Update application' # This event is triggered when secrets/certs are added
  filter_user_action:
    InitiatedBy.user.id|exists: true # Exclude actions taken by human users
  condition: selection and not filter_user_action
indicators.description: Detects persistence activity where an application principal adds new credentials to another application, as seen in the ConnectWise attack.
